theme: Priestly ordination; Nadab and Abihu, God’s holiness is not safe
readingInstruction: Read Leviticus 8:1-10:20. This reading includes the ordination of the priests, the first sacrifices, and a terrible event on the first day. Read the contrast between chapter 9 and chapter 10 carefully.
settingTheScene: The instructions in Leviticus 1 to 7 were given at Sinai. Now the narrative moves forward. In chapter 8, Moses carries out the ordination ceremony that was described in Exodus 29. In chapter 9, on the eighth day, the priests begin their ministry. In chapter 10, two of Aaron’s sons make an offering that God did not command, and they die. The sequence shows both the glory of God’s provision and the danger of approaching him on our own terms.
observation: Moses washes Aaron and his sons, dresses them, anoints them, and offers the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the ordination offering (8:1-30).
The priests must stay at the entrance of the tent for seven days, “so that you may not die” (8:33-35).
On the eighth day, Aaron offers the sacrifices for himself and for the people (9:1-21).
Aaron blesses the people, and “the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people” (9:22-23).
“Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar, and when all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces” (9:24).
Nadab and Abihu “offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them” (10:1).
“Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD” (10:2).
Moses says, “This is what the LORD has said: Among those who are near me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified” (10:3). “And Aaron held his peace.”
interpretation:
This is one of the hardest passages in the Old Testament, so take it slowly. It shows two sides of God. In chapter 9, the glory of God appears and fire from heaven accepts the sacrifice. The people shout and fall on their faces. It is an overwhelming scene of acceptance. God has provided a way, the priests have done what he commanded, and he has come down to be with them.

In chapter 10, the same fire that consumed the sacrifice consumes two priests. The difference is that Nadab and Abihu offered “unauthorized fire.” The text does not say exactly what was wrong with it. It says only that it was something God “had not commanded.” The lesson is more important than the details. God is not to be approached in just any way we choose. He has told us how to worship, and worship that goes beyond his word is dangerous.

The event happens on the very day the priesthood begins. It is a warning at the start. The text is saying that God’s holiness is not a matter of mood or ritual. It is who he is, and those who serve near him must take it seriously. Moses’ explanation is the key: “Among those who are near me I will be sanctified.” Those who are closest to God are held to the highest standard.

Aaron’s silence in the face of the loss of his sons is a moment of great restraint. He does not argue, and he does not accuse God. He holds his peace. It is a hard, quiet response to a hard event.

We must also remember that the story is not meant to tell us that God is arbitrary. The sacrifices were provided for exactly this reason: so that sinners could approach safely. The danger was not in the system but in ignoring it. Those who came in the way God had commanded were welcome. Those who came another way were not.
connection: Hebrews 12:28-29 says, “Let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe, for our God is a consuming fire.” Peter quotes the same theme, “Be holy, for I am holy” (1 Peter 1:16). The story of Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:1-11) echoes it, as the early church learned a similar lesson about deceit in worship. Jesus has made a new and living way open to us (Hebrews 10:19-20), and he is the way (John 14:6).
application:
Ask yourself whether you come to God in the way he has taught, through Christ and in his Word, or in a way that suits you.

Take a few minutes to think about the seriousness of worship. Come to church this week with reverence.

If you are grieving a loss, ask God to give you the quiet courage that Aaron showed.
prayerPrompts: Tell God what you think of when you hear that he is a consuming fire.
Thank him for the new and living way in Jesus.
Ask him to teach you to worship with reverence and awe.
